note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Calculate a student's final grade from weighted category scores. Homework counts 20%, quizzes 30%, the exam 50%. In the homework category the lowest score is dropped when there are 4 or more scores. Round the final grade to 1 decimal place.
facts: Made-up example: homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (drop 70, average 90), quizzes 80 and 70 (average 75), exam 60. Final = 0.2*90 + 0.3*75 + 0.5*60 = 70.5. A category with no scores counts as 0.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Final grade = 0.2 x homework average + 0.3 x quiz average + 0.5 x exam score. The weights total 100%.
REQ-2: Homework: if there are 4 or more scores, drop the single lowest score and average the rest. With fewer than 4 scores, average them all with no drop.
REQ-3: Any category with no scores counts as 0 in the formula.
REQ-4: Round the final grade to 1 decimal place and show it with that 1 decimal (for example 48.0). The brief does not say how to round exact halves (such as 70.25), so this needs confirming with the requester.
AC-1: Homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (drop 70, average 90); quizzes 80, 70 (average 75); exam 60. Final = 0.2 x 90 + 0.3 x 75 + 0.5 x 60 = 18 + 22.5 + 30 = 70.5.
AC-2: Homework 90, 80, 70 (3 scores, no drop, average 80); quizzes 80, 70 (average 75); exam 60. Final = 16 + 22.5 + 30 = 68.5.
AC-3: Homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (average 90 after the drop); no quiz scores (counts as 0); exam 60. Final = 18 + 0 + 30 = 48.0.
AC-4: Homework 80, 80, 85 (average 81.667); quizzes 70, 71 (average 70.5); exam 77. Final = 16.333 + 21.15 + 38.5 = 75.983, shown as 76.0.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Final grade equals 0.2 times the homework category score plus 0.3 times the quiz category score plus 0.5 times the exam score.
REQ-2: If homework has 4 or more scores, drop the lowest score before averaging; quizzes are averaged with no drop.
REQ-3: A category with no scores counts as 0.
REQ-4: Round the final grade to 1 decimal place.
AC-1: Homework 90, 80, 70, 100 drops 70 and averages 90; quizzes 80 and 70 average 75; exam 60; final is 0.2*90 + 0.3*75 + 0.5*60 = 70.5.
AC-2: With no quiz scores, the quiz category is 0, so the same homework and exam give 0.2*90 + 0.3*0 + 0.5*60 = 48.0.

reviewOfA.strengths: AC-1 matches the given example exactly, including dropping 70, averages of 90 and 75, and a final grade of 70.5.

REQ-1: Final grade = 0.2 x homework average + 0.3 x quiz average + 0.5 x exam score. The weights total 100%.
REQ-2: Homework: if there are 4 or more scores, drop the single lowest score and average the rest. If the lowest score is tied, drop only one of them. With fewer than 4 scores, average them all with no drop. Quizzes are averaged with no drop.
REQ-3: Any category with no scores counts as 0 in the formula.
REQ-4: Round the final grade to 1 decimal place and show it with that 1 decimal (for example 48.0). The brief does not say how to round exact halves (such as 70.25, which could become 70.3 or 70.2), so this needs confirming with the requester.
AC-1: Homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (drop 70, average 90); quizzes 80, 70 (average 75); exam 60. Final = 0.2 x 90 + 0.3 x 75 + 0.5 x 60 = 18 + 22.5 + 30 = 70.5.
AC-2: Homework 90, 80, 70 (3 scores, no drop, average 80); quizzes 80, 70 (average 75); exam 60. Final = 16 + 22.5 + 30 = 68.5.
AC-3: Homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (average 90 after the drop); no quiz scores (counts as 0); exam 60. Final = 18 + 0 + 30 = 48.0.
AC-4: Homework 80, 80, 85 (average 81.667); quizzes 70, 71 (average 70.5); exam 77. Final = 16.333 + 21.15 + 38.5 = 75.983, shown as 76.0.

merge.keptFromB: From Draft B I kept the explicit statement that quizzes are averaged with no drop, and I added a tie rule prompted by its review.

finalReview.strengths: AC-1 matches the given example exactly at 70.5, and the other cases correctly apply the 20/30/50 weights, the drop-at-4 rule, and a zero for an empty category.

build.contract: finalGrade(input) where input = { homework: number[], quizzes: number[], exam: number[] } (scores from 0 to 100; exam holds the single exam score, or is empty when there is none). Returns { homeworkAverage: number, quizAverage: number, examScore: number, final: number (rounded to 1 decimal place, such as 70.5), display: string (the final grade always written with 1 decimal, such as "48.0"), droppedHomework: number | null (the dropped lowest homework score; null when nothing was dropped) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field. Open item: the rounding of an unrounded final that sits exactly halfway between two 1-decimal values (for example 70.25 becoming 70.3 or 70.2) is not yet decided. It is pending confirmation with the requester under REQ-4. Until it is confirmed, final and display are specified only for values that are not exact halves, and tests must not assert an expected result for an exact-half case.

architecture.draft:
Components: one pure module finalGrade(input) built from small helpers: validateInput (throws Error "unknown field: <name>" for any key other than homework, quizzes or exam), average(scores) (returns 0 for an empty list), homeworkAverage(scores) (drops one lowest score only when there are 4 or more), weightedTotal, and roundTo1 plus formatDisplay.
Data: input { homework: number[], quizzes: number[], exam: number[] }. Output { homeworkAverage, quizAverage, examScore, final, display, droppedHomework }. Weights are constants 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5, which total 1.0.
Homework: if length >= 4, droppedHomework = min(scores) and one instance is removed, even when tied (AC-1 drops 70). Otherwise droppedHomework = null and all scores are averaged (AC-2 averages to 80).
Empty category: average, or examScore, is 0 (REQ-3, AC-3 gives 18 + 0 + 30 = 48.0). examScore = exam[0] when the array is present, else 0.
Rounding: keep it in one function, roundTo1, so the pending exact-half rule (REQ-4) changes only that function. display = final.toFixed(1), giving "48.0" and "76.0" (AC-4 gives 16.333 + 21.15 + 38.5 = 75.983, which becomes 76.0).
Float care: compute the unrounded total in full precision and round only once at the end. Example values checked: 70.5, 68.5, 48.0 and 76.0 are all correct.
Open items for the contract owner: (1) behavior when exam has more than 1 score; (2) a missing field (treat as empty, or throw?); (3) scores outside 0 to 100 or non-numbers (no error is specified).
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4, the tied-lowest drop, the unknown-field error, and all categories empty (final 0, display "0.0"). No assertion for exact-half cases.
File fence (paths assumed, as no repo layout was given): src/grade/finalGrade.js (new) and test/grade/finalGrade.test.js (new). No other files may change.
architecture.review:
AR-1 · P0 · Empty exam is not zero
  REQ-3 requires a category with no scores to count as 0. This line uses exam[0] whenever the exam array is present. An empty array is present, so exam[0] is undefined, not 0, and the final grade is wrong whenever there is no exam.
Strengths: Weights stay 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5, and the total is rounded only once at the end, so 70.5, 68.5, 48.0 and 76.0 remain correct.
architecture.final:
Components: one pure module finalGrade(input) built from helpers: validateInput (throws Error "unknown field: <name>" for any key other than homework, quizzes or exam), average(scores) (0 for an empty list), homeworkAverage(scores) (drops one lowest only when there are 4 or more), weightedTotal, roundTo1, formatDisplay.
Data: input { homework: number[], quizzes: number[], exam: number[] }. Output { homeworkAverage, quizAverage, examScore, final, display, droppedHomework }. Weights are constants 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5 (total 1.0).
Homework: if length >= 4, droppedHomework = min(scores) and only one instance is removed, even when tied (AC-1 drops 70, average 90). Otherwise droppedHomework = null and all scores are averaged (AC-2 gives 80).
Empty category: examScore = exam.length > 0 ? exam[0] : 0, so an empty exam array gives 0, not undefined (REQ-3). An empty homework or quiz list averages to 0 (AC-3: 18 + 0 + 30 = 48.0).
Rounding: only roundTo1 rounds, so the pending exact-half rule (REQ-4) changes only that function. display = final.toFixed(1), giving "48.0" and "76.0".
Float care: compute the unrounded total in full precision and round once at the end (AC-4: 16.333 + 21.15 + 38.5 = 75.983, shown as 76.0). Checked results: 70.5, 68.5, 48.0 and 76.0.
Open items for the contract owner: (1) exam with more than 1 score; (2) a missing field (treat as empty or throw?); (3) scores outside 0 to 100 or non-numbers (no error is specified).
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4; the tied-lowest drop; the unknown-field error; an empty exam (homework 90, 80, 70, 100; quizzes 80, 70; exam [] gives 18 + 22.5 + 0 = 40.5, examScore 0); all categories empty (final 0, display "0.0"). No assertion for exact-half cases.
File fence (paths assumed, as no repo layout was given): src/grade/finalGrade.js (new) and test/grade/finalGrade.test.js (new). No other files may change.
architecture.resolutions: AR-1 · P0 · Empty exam is not zero applied: examScore now uses exam.length > 0 ? exam[0] : 0, so an empty exam counts as 0 under REQ-3. Added an empty-exam test: 18 + 22.5 + 0 = 40.5.

code.summary: This module computes the final grade with the weights 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5 from the PRD. It drops one lowest homework score only when there are 4 or more, and only one copy when the lowest is tied. A category with no scores counts as 0, and the exam score is the first entry in the exam array. Any key other than homework, quizzes or exam throws "unknown field: <name>". The total is kept at full precision and rounded once, in roundTo1 only, using Math.round(x*10)/10. Display uses toFixed(1). I checked the cases by hand: AC-1 gives 70.5, AC-2 68.5, AC-3 48.0, AC-4 75.983 shown as 76.0, the empty exam case 40.5, and all categories empty gives 0.0. Exact-half rounding (REQ-4) is still pending with the requester. The current behaviour should not be treated as specified, and changing it means editing roundTo1 only. Four choices I made where the contract is silent: (1) A missing field or a non-array value is treated as an empty list. (2) A non-object input throws a generic error, not the unknown-field message. (3) An exam with more than 1 score uses only the first and ignores the rest silently. (4) Scores outside 0 to 100 or non-numbers are not checked. All four are still open items for the contract owner.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Full-precision category averages and one 1-decimal round reproduce the acceptance results 70.5, 68.5, 48.0, and 76.0.
code.resolutions: Review reports no defects; the full-precision averages with a single 1-decimal round reproduce AC results 70.5, 68.5, 48.0 and 76.0. applied: I agree and have checked each case myself. AC-1: 18 + 22.5 + 30 = 70.5. AC-2: 16 + 22.5 + 30 = 68.5. AC-3: 18 + 0 + 30 = 48, displayed as 48.0. AC-4: 16.333 + 21.15 + 38.5 = 75.983, rounded to 76.0. Homework drops only one tied lowest score, and only when there are 4 or more scores. Empty categories count as 0. Any field other than homework, quizzes or exam throws 'unknown field: <name>'. Exact-half rounding is still the open item under REQ-4. The code applies Math.round there, but no test should assert an exact-half result until the requester confirms. The code is unchanged.
